spendguard/cachetest.py::_run_calls::max.why: The code ignores the reply's content and only reads r.usage.prompt_tokens_details, making this a cache-behaviour probe where the generated text is discarded.
The code only reads m.usage (token/cache accounting) from each response and never consumes m.content or the reply text, which is characteristic of a cache-behaviour probe.

spendguard/refresh.py::_llm_lookup::max_.why: The call uses a web_search tool and returns a message whose content is evidently consumed as the lookup result for the refresh operation, so a truncated reply would be silently parsed as wrong or empty data.

spendguard/vendor_call.py::discover_effo.why: The call sends a fixed "Reply: OK" prompt and the code only reads r.get("error") to test which reasoning-effort values connect, discarding the actual reply content.

spendguard/verify.py::_probe_failover::m.why: The code only checks that the reply has nonempty text and came from the API without an error; it does not consume the text's content.
